item.title: The Killer Who Saw Unlocked Doors As An Invitation
item.description: Richard Chase told investigators he viewed unlocked doors as invitations to enter. Known as the “Vampire of Sacramento,” he killed six people in 1977–78. He was convicted of six first-degree murders in 1979 and sentenced to death.

item.title: Her Voice Notes Warned She Was Capable Of Killing Him
item.description: Abigail White, known online as “Fake Barbie,” killed Bradley Lewis, 22, in Kingswood, England, in March 2022. Jurors heard earlier voice notes in which she said she was capable of killing him. Convicted of murder that October, she received life imprisonment with a minimum term of 18 years.

item.title: She Survived A Motorway Collision, Then Killed Her Host
item.description: In 2008, twins Sabina and Ursula Eriksson survived running into traffic on England’s M6. After her release from custody, Sabina killed Glenn Hollinshead, who had offered her somewhere to stay. She pleaded guilty to manslaughter on grounds of diminished responsibility and received five years in prison.

item.title: A Letter Sent To The Wrong Address Exposed A Killer
item.description: A survivor’s letter describing Peter Kürten’s attack reached the wrong address—and then police, helping identify the serial killer known as the “Vampire of Düsseldorf.” He was convicted of nine murders and executed in 1931.

item.title: His Final Murders Exposed A 33-Year Family Secret
item.description: Charlie Brandt killed his wife, Teri, and niece Michelle Jones in Florida in 2004 before dying by suicide. The investigation uncovered his family's hidden history: at 13, he had killed his mother. His younger sisters had been told she died in a car accident.

item.title: He Hid His Roommate’s Remains In A Bus Terminal
item.description: After Swiss dance student Monika Beerle was killed in 1989, police found her remains at New York’s Port Authority Bus Terminal. Her roommate, Daniel Rakowitz, was found not guilty by reason of insanity in 1991 and committed to a secure psychiatric hospital

item.title: A Phone Monitoring App Exposed His Teacher’s Abuse
item.description: Arizona teacher Brittany Zamora’s abuse of a 13-year-old student came to light when his parents checked his phone using a monitoring app. She tried to persuade them not to contact police. In 2019, she pleaded guilty and was sentenced to 20 years in prison.
